email.subject1: pipeline Blue Ridge is leaving on the table
email.body1:
Matthew, saw Blue Ridge launched Blu, your GenAI Forecasting Companion, this past October.

A category move like that usually creates more in-market accounts than the team can cover before competitors answer it. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Blue Ridge off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Matthew, quick follow-up for Blue Ridge.

As CRO, you're carrying the number on the Blu launch, but headcount rarely scales as fast as the demand a launch creates. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book to convert that interest, so the gap surfaces late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Blue Ridge needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Matthew, last bit of proof for Blue Ridge.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Blue Ridge's reply rate likely compares to other supply-chain software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Matthew, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a CRO priority while Blu rolls out, no problem at all. Timing is everything around a launch, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Blue Ridge either way.
